newsitem.title: GERMANY: German grain intervention offers detailed-Toepfer.
newsitem.headline: German grain intervention offers detailed-Toepfer.

text.p: Final German offers in the 1996/97 (Nov/May) grain intervention season totalled 1.57 million tonnes versus 1.68 million tonnes in 95/96, grain trader Alfred C Toepfer said in its monthly market report.
The report, which excluded small volumes of maize, said the volume was significantly lower than expected.
Offers are volumes accepted, but not yet delivered to stores.
They may be withdrawn or rejected on quality grounds, but a source at Toepfer said fluctuations in the tonnage likely to be delivered to stores should not be too high.
Toepfer offered the following break-down of rounded figures -- soft wheat 250,000 tonnes (10,000 tonnes last season), barley 550,000 tonnes (730,000), rye 770,000 (940,000).
Traders said uncertainty in the grain market had caused a last minute rush into intervention, especially in wheat, after the season had been sluggish all along.
The May buying-in price for all grains was 248.61 marks/tonne.
